transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
My mind just doesn’t seem to work the way it used to—I can’t think straight or make simple decisions anymore. It's just so exhausting, and I feel completely stuck trying to do basic everyday things.

Have these memory and concentration problems been causing major difficulty with your daily life, like work, managing money, or taking care of yourself? Or are they more of a mild annoyance without much impact on your functioning?

Oh, it's definitely a major difficulty, and I just don't feel capable of handling my everyday responsibilities anymore. I’ve had to stop going to my art and quilting groups, and I'm falling behind on paying my bills. I even missed an important medication refill and some appointments for my sister because of this mental fogginess.
Have you also been feeling so depressed that you can’t get through most of the day, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like there’s just no point to the day. I've also completely lost interest in my watercolor classes, quilting, and genealogy trips, because trying to go and enjoy them just feels like way too much effort now.
Have you been having major changes in your sleep, such as sleeping much more or much less than usual?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep patterns. For the most part, my sleep has been relatively normal, even if I still wake up feeling very heavy and tired in the morning.
Have you had any experiences like hearing voices other people don’t hear, or strong beliefs that others would say are not true, such as feeling watched, controlled, or guilty beyond reason?

I don't hear any voices, but I've been convinced for a while that some of the doctors and nurses at my sister's hospital are quietly working against us. I feel like they are changing her charts and delaying things on purpose because I must have done something wrong, even though everyone keeps telling me there's no proof of that at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a depressive syndrome with marked anhedonia, persistent low mood/heavy sinking feeling, prominent psychomotor/cognitive slowing and impaired concentration, and clear functional impairment in daily responsibilities. She also reports mood-congruent persecutory/guilt-based delusional beliefs about hospital staff sabotaging her sister's care and that she must have done something wrong, with no hallucinations. This supports a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
